units.text: INT. CONVALESCENT HOME SOLARIUM - AFTERNOON
A glass-walled room full of wicker chairs and ferns.
Pale sun.
Somewhere down the corridor, a gramophone plays a waltz.
DR. HORATIO PEMBERTON-LAW, 50s, in a rumpled tweed jacket, stands by the window with his hat in his hand.
MRS. EUPHEMIA STANHOPE-ADEYEMI, 80s, in a shawl and a wheelchair, faces the garden.
Her hands rest on a blanket.
Good afternoon, Mrs. Stanhope-Adeyemi.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Good afternoon, Doctor. You are late.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: The train was held up.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Trains always are.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: He pulls up a wicker chair.
Sits.
Opens his bag.
Closes it again without taking anything out.
You are looking well.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: I am looking at the roses.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: They are fine roses.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: They are blighted. The gardener lies.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: Perhaps he is hopeful.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Perhaps he is paid by the hour.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: Horatio smiles.
Smooths his hat.
A nurse's shoe squeaks past in the corridor and fades.
I have the results.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: I supposed you might.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: They are not what we hoped.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Are they ever?
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: He takes a sheet of paper from his jacket.
Offers it.
She doesn't take it.
Instead she reaches out and presses his hand, paper and all, down onto the blanket.
Read it to the roses, Doctor. They've heard worse.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: Mrs. Stanhope-Adeyemi--
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Euphemia. I am too old to be called anything else by a man I like.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: He sets the paper on his knee.
Does not read it.
I should like to come on Thursdays.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: You come on Mondays.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: Then Thursdays also.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: I shall tell the gardener.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: About the Thursdays?
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: About the roses. He ought to be told.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: They both go still.
Horatio looks at the paper; Euphemia looks at the glass.
Neither looks at the other.
Down the corridor the waltz ends.
The gramophone needle hisses in the empty groove.
Euphemia lifts one finger, listening.
They always forget to turn it over.
units.name: EUPHEMIA

units.text: Horatio stands, crosses to the door, and calls softly down the hall.
Would someone turn the record, please?
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: He returns to the chair.
A moment later the music resumes, soft and a little slow.
